title: A matrix moves the whole plane

beats.text: What does a matrix do to this arrow? Its coordinates, two and one, mean two steps across and one step up.
Call the two unit directions e one and e two. Our arrow is two copies of e one, plus one copy of e two.
Choose a transformation. Send e one to two, one. Send e two to one, two. Those destinations become the two columns of our matrix.
Where will our original arrow land? Watch the whole grid transform. The arrow and the unit square follow the same map.
Keep the same recipe in the new directions. Two copies of two, one, plus one copy of one, two. Add the contributions: the result is five, four.
The unit square now has area three. The determinant gives that signed area scale. A linear map fixes the origin and keeps parallel lines parallel.
